Compute Summary Statistics for Covariate Forest Plots

Source: R/plot_forest.R
df_forest.Rd

Summarizes replicate draws for each metric and covariate level into a median and a ci percentile interval, with formatted labels, and returns a forest_stats object for plot_forest() / plot_build_forest(). Rows are in plot order, top to bottom; reorder stats$stats to change it. One object draws either reference layout (see ref_layout in plot_build_forest()) without re-aggregating.

Usage

df_forest(
  data,
  metric_name_var = "metric",
  metric_value_var = "value",
  cov_name_var = "cov_name",
  cov_level_var = "cov_level",
  ci = 0.9,
  sigdigits = 3,
  cov_name_ref = "Reference",
  cov_level_ref = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Input data.frame. Replicate level long format dataset: one row per metric, covariate, covariate level, and replicate.

metric_name_var

Column in data containing metric names. Accepts bare names or strings. Default is metric.

metric_value_var

Column in data containing replicate draws of the test/reference comparison statistic. Accepts bare names or strings. Default value.

cov_name_var

Column in data containing covariate variable names. (e.g., WTBL,FOOD, etc). Accepts bare names or strings. Default is cov_name.

cov_level_var

Column in data containing covariate levels (e.g., 70 kg). Accepts bare names or strings. Default is cov_level.

ci

Numeric scalar in (0, 1) specifying the central interval width (e.g., 0.9 for 90% CI).

sigdigits

Number of significant digits used to format the label columns. Digits are counted on the median estimate of each metric, which fixes one count of decimal places for every value of that metric ("1.00", "0.95", "2.32" for a ratio; "12500", "9500" for an exposure near 12500). Trailing zeros are kept. Default 3.

cov_name_ref

The value of cov_name_var that marks the reference rows, drawn in the reference panel at the top. Default "Reference", as in df_forest_preprocess() output; NULL for no reference row.

cov_level_ref

Optional named vector of per-covariate reference labels, e.g. c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg"). When given, the reference row is also drawn inside each named covariate panel under that label, and this becomes the default ref_layout. Unnamed covariates show no reference row. Requires cov_name_ref. Default NULL (reference panel only).

Value

A forest_stats container (subclass of pmx_stats) with three slots:

stats

One row per plotted point, in display order, with character columns named in metric_name_var / cov_name_var / cov_level_var, canonical numeric columns est (median of the draws), lo, hi (the (1 - ci) / 2 and 1 - (1 - ci) / 2 percentiles), the integer n (the number of non-NA draws behind the row), the character columns est_label, lo_label, and hi_label (those values formatted per sigdigits), ci_label (the three combined for tables, e.g. "1.12 (0.95, 1.32)"), the logical is_ref, and layout, the reference layout(s) a row draws in: "both" (covariate rows), "consolidated" (the reference panel), or "distributed" (the reference copies placed in each cov_level_ref covariate). The cov_name_var value drives the per-row facet strip; the cov_level_var value drives the y-axis tick label; plot_build_forest() assembles est_label, lo_label, and hi_label into the right-hand secondary y-axis text, so edit those columns (not ci_label) to change the plotted text.

obs

NULL. No scatter overlay for the forest family.

config

Named list with column names, ci, sigdigits, cov_name_ref, and cov_level_ref.

Pass directly to plot_forest() or plot_build_forest() to render.

Reference rows

Reference rows are flagged is_ref and drawn through the ref_point style role. With cov_level_ref, stats$stats holds both the reference-panel rows and a copy in each named covariate panel, told apart by the layout column. cov_level_ref names not found in cov_name_var, or naming the reference itself, are ignored with a warning; a label equal to an existing level of that covariate also warns, since both rows would share it.

Row order

Rows of stats$stats are sorted into display order, top to bottom: metrics and covariates follow their factor levels when the input columns are factors, otherwise their order of first appearance in data, with the reference panel moved first. Within a covariate, factor levels of cov_level_var win when they cover every label (including the covariate's reference label); otherwise, if every label carries a distinct number, labels sort ascending by it, sign included (50 kg above 90 kg); any other set puts the reference label on top followed by the data order. The reference copies are placed by the same rules, so the covariate rows keep one order in both layouts.

See also

Other forest plot: df_forest_preprocess(), is_forest_stats(), plot_build_forest(), plot_forest(), style_forest(), style_forest_coveffectsplot(), style_forest_pmforest(), style_forest_pmxforest(), style_forest_pumas()

Examples

# Aggregate replicate simulations to point estimate + 90% CI
df_forest(dplyr::filter(data_sad_pkforest, grepl("RATIO$", metric)))
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 24 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Reference, cov_level_ref = NULL
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>      metric  cov_name cov_level      est       lo       hi   n est_label
#> 1 CMAXRATIO Reference Reference 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 500      1.00
#> 2 CMAXRATIO      FOOD       Fed 1.702998 1.444680 2.021474 500      1.70
#> 3 CMAXRATIO      WTBL     50 kg 1.297623 1.216627 1.388727 500      1.30
#>   lo_label hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1     1.00     1.00 1.00 (1.00, 1.00)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2     1.44     2.02 1.70 (1.44, 2.02)  FALSE         both
#> 3     1.22     1.39 1.30 (1.22, 1.39)  FALSE         both
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.

# A reference named something other than "Reference"
renamed <- dplyr::mutate(
  data_sad_pkforest,
  cov_level = ifelse(cov_name == "Reference", "70 kg, fasted", cov_level),
  cov_name = ifelse(cov_name == "Reference", "Typical subject", cov_name)
)
df_forest(renamed, cov_name_ref = "Typical subject")
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 48 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Typical subject, cov_level_ref = NULL
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>   metric        cov_name     cov_level       est        lo       hi   n
#> 1   CMAX Typical subject 70 kg, fasted  861.3751  741.2410 1005.205 500
#> 2   CMAX            FOOD           Fed 1465.1054 1180.1763 1830.221 500
#> 3   CMAX            WTBL         50 kg 1118.5361  936.4438 1306.034 500
#>   est_label lo_label hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1       861      741     1005   861 (741, 1005)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2      1465     1180     1830 1465 (1180, 1830)  FALSE         both
#> 3      1119      936     1306  1119 (936, 1306)  FALSE         both
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.

# Per-covariate reference labels (the dataset's attribute,
# c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg")): the reference row is drawn in each
# covariate panel
df_forest(
  dplyr::filter(data_sad_pkforest, metric == "AUCRATIO"),
  cov_level_ref = attr(data_sad_pkforest, "cov_level_ref")
)
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 8 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Reference, cov_level_ref = c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg")
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>     metric  cov_name cov_level      est       lo       hi   n est_label
#> 1 AUCRATIO Reference Reference 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 500      1.00
#> 2 AUCRATIO      FOOD    Fasted 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 500      1.00
#> 3 AUCRATIO      FOOD       Fed 2.316439 2.004453 2.648564 500      2.32
#>   lo_label hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1     1.00     1.00 1.00 (1.00, 1.00)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2     1.00     1.00 1.00 (1.00, 1.00)   TRUE  distributed
#> 3     2.00     2.65 2.32 (2.00, 2.65)  FALSE         both
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.

# Control the row order with factor levels on the input
d <- dplyr::filter(data_sad_pkforest, metric == "AUCRATIO")
d$cov_level <- factor(d$cov_level, levels = c("Reference", "Fed", "Fasted",
                                          "50 kg", "70 kg", "90 kg"))
df_forest(d, cov_level_ref = attr(data_sad_pkforest, "cov_level_ref"))
#> <forest_stats>
#>   stats: 7 rows x 13 columns
#>   config: metric_name_var = metric, metric_value_var = value, cov_name_var = cov_name, cov_level_var = cov_level, ci = 0.9, sigdigits = 3, cov_name_ref = Reference, cov_level_ref = c(FOOD = "Fasted", WTBL = "70 kg")
#> 
#>   head(stats, 3):
#>     metric  cov_name cov_level      est       lo       hi   n est_label
#> 1 AUCRATIO Reference Reference 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 500      1.00
#> 2 AUCRATIO      FOOD       Fed 2.316439 2.004453 2.648564 500      2.32
#> 3 AUCRATIO      FOOD    Fasted 1.000000 1.000000 1.000000 500      1.00
#>   lo_label hi_label          ci_label is_ref       layout
#> 1     1.00     1.00 1.00 (1.00, 1.00)   TRUE consolidated
#> 2     2.00     2.65 2.32 (2.00, 2.65)  FALSE         both
#> 3     1.00     1.00 1.00 (1.00, 1.00)   TRUE  distributed
#> 
#>   Use `x$stats` for the full data.frame.
